q1_issues.issue: The add-event roles are mis-slotted: the direct object "about $215 million" gets no role filler at all (it is demoted to a Measure on the event), and "to Kodak's revenue" — a to-PP, hence Goal or Recipient — is put in Patient, so the revenue is recorded as the thing added rather than as what it is added to.

(Degree sk_dilutive_1 dilutive slightly) puts the reified state witness in the bearer slot; Degree's first argument is the entity that has the property ((Degree alice tall very)), so this should bear on sk_acquisition_1.

(Of sk_acquisition_1 practiceworks) invents a preposition that is not in the surface — "the PracticeWorks acquisition" is a noun-noun compound with no "of", and the head must be the preposition actually used.

(Time sk_add_1 first_full_year) coins a three-word symbol for "in the first full year" with no decomposition; a Time filler must be a structured calendar term, a deictic, or a named time, and this is none of them.

q2_gaps: a proper-noun modifier naming a PARTICIPANT of a deverbal head noun ("the PracticeWorks acquisition" = the acquisition of PracticeWorks) — the compound rules explicitly do not apply to proper nouns, the name+kind pattern ("the Brindle estuary") is for a name that IS the thing, and there is no surface preposition to hang an oblique on

an ordinal-described relative time span ("in the first full year") — Time terms are calendar granularities, deictics, or named times, none of which covers a span picked out by rank relative to an unstated anchor

a relative-polarity financial predicate contrasted across two time spans ("dilutive through 2005, accretive thereafter") — dual-emit forces both flat copular atoms out, and inside one seal they read as simultaneously true
notes: The impersonal-reported-attitude routing is right — expect reified with no Experiencer, content sealed under Theme, subject typing and the definite "Kodak's revenue" projected at top level, no tense inside the non-finite complement — and the approximation (ParticleFromNormal 215000000 21500000) applies the 10%-sigma tight-hedge rule correctly. The two flat atoms (Member sk_acquisition_1 dilutive) and (Member sk_acquisition_1 accretive) contradict each other inside one seal, but that follows the dual-emit instruction as written.
